answer: An agent economy resists sybil attacks by requiring every identity to carry a verifiable record of real work, and by making that record impossible to mass-produce. A newcomer enters an open meadow where nothing is granted: it must fell its own timber, one honest contribution at a time, before building any standing. The kernel of reputation at each account's center is peer-attested and cannot be copied, lent, or bought in bulk. A farm minting ten thousand keys ends up with ten thousand empty shells, none able to vote, since weight flows from earned tenure, not account count.
